page.tested_text: We rendered all ten, and the reel you watched is made of them. **Not checked on a clean computer:** the five set-up steps follow Remotion's own guide, but we ran the moves inside our existing project.
page.tip: **The tip:** start with one move. Change its words, render it, then add the next.

prompt: I'm making short vertical animations for social media with Remotion (React). For each animation I describe, write ONE self-contained component in one file that only imports from 'remotion'. Size 1080 x 1920, 30 frames a second, about 2 seconds long. Animate it only with useCurrentFrame() and interpolate(): no CSS animations and no extra packages. Look: off-white background #F6F4EF, white cards with a thin 2.5px near-black outline, rounded corners and a soft shadow, one accent colour #00D97E, red #E5484D only for mistakes, heavy sans-serif type. Keep everything in the middle of the frame and add short comments in plain English. Then give me the one line that registers it in Root.tsx and the command that renders it as an mp4. First animation: a red stamp that says WRONG slams onto a chat card and shakes it.

followups.label: Time it to your voice
followups.prompt: Add a prop called at, in seconds, so I can choose the exact moment the stamp lands. I'll set it to a word in my voice-over.
followups.note: Every move below already has a timing prop like this. It's how each one lands on its word in the reel.

followups.label: Make it yours
followups.prompt: Keep the motion exactly the same, but use my colours: background [hex], accent [hex]. And change the words on screen to: [your words].
followups.note: The words, numbers and colours are props or constants at the top of each file, so this is a small change.

followups.label: Join two moves
followups.prompt: Play the stamp for 2 seconds, then the gauge for 2 seconds, in one video. Use Remotion's Series component.
followups.note: This is how the reel plays all ten back to back.

checklist.title: Install Node.js
checklist.detail: Free, from nodejs.org. Pick the LTS version. On a Mac you need macOS 15 or later.

checklist.title: Make a project
checklist.detail: In Terminal: npx create-video@latest --yes --blank my-video, then cd my-video.

checklist.title: Add a move
checklist.detail: Save its code as src/Stamp.jsx. Import it in src/Root.tsx and add the Composition line from the top of the file.

checklist.title: Watch it
checklist.detail: npm run dev opens the preview in your browser. Change a number and it updates.

checklist.title: Export the video
checklist.detail: npx remotion render Stamp out/stamp.mp4 gives you the file.

safety: **Remotion is free** for individuals and companies of up to 3 people. Bigger companies need a paid licence (remotion.dev/license).
**Claude's free plan** can write this code. We used Claude Code, which comes with a paid plan.
**The voice is separate.** Claude made the animation, not the voice. Record your own, or try a text-to-speech tool: ElevenLabs has a free plan for testing (no commercial licence on it).

**On a Claude Team or Enterprise plan?** Claude Motion (type /motion in the chat) makes animations inside Claude and exports an MP4. It is in beta on those plans only, so this kit is the free route for everyone else.

library.label: step 4 · the ten moves
library.title: All ten prompts, plus the code
library.intro: Each move has its plain-English brief and the code Claude wrote for it. Nine of them play in the reel; all ten are here.

items.name: The stamp
items.prompt: A chat card sits in the middle: a grey bubble on the right asks "Help me write a breakup text..." and a reply types out under it. At 0.9 seconds a red stamp that says WRONG slams onto the card: it starts 2.2 times too big, lands in a fifth of a second, tilted 7 degrees, and the card wobbles for half a second. Give me props for the stamp's word and the moment it lands.

items.name: The switch
items.prompt: A big switch in the middle, with a small label above it and the word On below. A mouse cursor glides in from the bottom right and clicks the switch at 1 second, dipping as it clicks. The knob slides left, the track fades from green to grey, the word changes to Off, and a green tick pops next to it. Give me a prop for the moment it flips.

items.name: The gauge
items.prompt: A white card with a half-circle dial. The needle sweeps from 0 to 7 out of 10 in about a second, a green arc fills in behind the needle, and the big number under it counts up with the needle. Give me props for the score and the timing.

items.name: The chart that draws itself
items.prompt: A white card with a small label, a big number and a line chart. The line draws itself from left to right while the number counts from 1,000 to 1,400. When it finishes, a green badge that says +40% pops in next to the number, slightly tilted. Give me props for the two numbers and the badge.

items.name: The heart monitor
items.prompt: A dark rounded panel with a heart-monitor line scrolling across it and a big number on the right. It starts red at 138 beats a minute, with tall, fast beats. At 0.9 seconds it calms down over half a second to 72: the beats get slower and smaller and everything turns green. Draw the line with a maths function, not an image.

items.name: The bingo card
items.prompt: A bingo card: a title bar and a 3 by 3 grid of job-interview clichés like "Hard worker" and "Team player". The three boxes in the top row turn green one by one, each with a little bump. Then a red BINGO stamp slams across the card and the card shakes. Give me props for the words and the timing.

items.name: The magnifier
items.prompt: A page of small print: a few grey lines and one real sentence, "Reviewed chats can be kept for up to three years." A magnifying glass glides along that sentence from left to right, and inside the glass the words are 2.4 times bigger, like a real lens. Do it by drawing the page twice: the bigger copy only shows through the round lens.

items.name: The year roller
items.prompt: A white card with a small label and one huge year. The year rolls upward like a slot machine from 2026 to 2029, blurred while it moves. As it stops, a red stamp that says "3 years" lands on the top right corner. Give me props for the list of years and the stamp.

items.name: The wall of cards
items.prompt: Twelve small white cards in a 3 by 4 grid, each with a short request like "Rewrite my CV". They pop in as a wave that starts in the middle. At 1.15 seconds every card flies into the centre and shrinks away, and one black rounded tile appears there showing the number 12 in green and the word "chats".

items.name: The phone that taps itself
items.prompt: A phone in the middle of the frame that taps itself through three screens. Screen one is a menu: the "Settings" row lights up green as if tapped and the next screen slides in from the right. Screen two is Settings: "Data controls" lights up and the last screen slides in. On the last screen a switch flips from on to off and a big green tick pops. No finger and no cursor.
